messages:
kira: Hey team — noticing a bad jump on the 'quickstart' page when you click the 'Example: streaming' anchor. The codeblock has a trailing backslash and the generated id ends up with a literal backslash in it and linkcheck flags a broken fragment.

ben: Can you paste the snippet? I think I saw something similar when a fenced code block ends immediately after a list item.

kira: Minimal repro in the MDX: 
```mdx
- Example
```bash
redwood stream --live \\\n```
- Next bullet
```

ben: Ah yeah — that trailing escaped backslash inside the fenced block is leaking into the slug generator somehow on the mkdocs build. Docusaurus was more forgiving and normalized it away, but mkdocs kept the backslash when creating the id.

deploy-bot: build failed — mkdocs-linkcheck: Broken fragment /docs/quickstart#example-streaming-\\ -> 1 error.

emily: Quick workaround: remove the trailing backslash or add a blank line after the fence. But we should sanitize code fences for slug generation rather than forcing authors to change content.

carol: I vote for the remark preprocess approach: strip trailing backslashes and other escape noise from nodes that influence heading/codeblock adjacent slugs. Also add a lint rule that warns on code fences ending with escape chars.

ben: Agreed. I'll prototype a remark plugin that normalizes nearby list/code fence pairs: it will trim trailing backslashes inside code fences and ensure empty list bullets are handled. Also produces a mapping of original->canonical slug so we can emit alias ids.

kira: Can you also grep for suspicious fences? Something like `git grep -n "\\\\$" -- docs | sed -E 's/:.*$//' | sort -u` should show files with trailing backslashes. I found 6 pages in guides and examples.

ben: Good find. I'll include repo fixes for those 6 files and add a lint rule to fail CI if a fenced block ends with an escape char.

deploy-bot: CI queued for PR 4899 (code-fence escape normalizer + lint + fixes).

emily: When you add alias ids, can we prefer canonical slugs without the escapes and add a short redirect shim on the site so bookmarked anchors with raw backslashes keep working? Some external blogs already link to the old anchors.

ben: Yep — plan: 1) canonicalize slugs in build, 2) emit HTML alias ids for historic slugs, 3) add _redirects entries for the worst offenders, 4) lint/auto-fix the repo hits.

deploy-bot: CI update: build started for PR 4899 (mkdocs + linkcheck).

carol: I added a unit test for the normalizer: `normalizeFence("redwood stream --live \") -> "redwood stream --live"` and a snapshot asserting the generated anchor is `example-streaming-live`.

emily: Local linkcheck after fixes: 6 -> 0 broken fragments. Added migration note in docs/migration.md explaining the change and telling authors how to avoid the pattern.

deploy-bot: Build passed for PR 4899 :white_check_mark: linkcheck OK.

kira: Merged. Thanks everyone! I'll follow up to update CONTRIBUTING.md with a short authoring tip about trailing escapes in examples.

ben: Nice teamwork. Closing this thread unless regressions surface. :wave:
